HBR: "To Scale AI Agents Successfully, Think of Them Like Team Members"

April 7, 2026 · Chris O'Hara

Telang, Hydari, and Iqbal from Carnegie Mellon and Pitt published this on March 23, and it's the most useful framework we've seen for positioning AI governance.

The Framework

The core insight is simple and sticky: every AI agent needs the same governance infrastructure you apply to a human employee.

The Five Requirements for Every AI Agent

1
Defined Identity — Who is this agent, and what is it accountable for?
2
Bounded Authority — What can it do, and what requires escalation?
3
Trusted Data Sources — What information does it have access to?
4
Execution Controls — What guardrails prevent it from going off-script?
5
Audit Trails — How do you trace what it did and why?

Why This Matters for SAP's Story

The "digital employee" framing maps directly to SAP's AI Agent Hub and lifecycle management story. It gives PMMs a third-party intellectual framework to reference when positioning governance — not just SAP talking points, but academic validation from Carnegie Mellon and Pitt.

6%

of companies fully trust AI agents for core processes

Source: Fortune

That stat makes the HBR framework feel urgent rather than theoretical. The market is adopting agents faster than it can govern them.

Practical Advice for PMMs

The HBR Recommendations

  • Treat new agents like interns, not full-time hires — limited scope, supervised execution, gradual trust-building
  • Give each agent a named human owner — someone accountable for its behavior
  • Review on a regular cycle — performance evaluations for your digital workforce

This is the kind of concrete guidance that makes PMMs sharpen their own messaging. When you're positioning SAP's governance capabilities, you can reference this framework: "Just like the HBR piece recommends, the AI Agent Hub gives every agent a defined identity, bounded authority, and full audit trail."

The Bottom Line

Both the Verasight data (64% adoption, 56% anxiety) and the HBR framework reinforce the same thread: the market is adopting agents faster than it can govern them, and the companies that solve the trust gap win.

That's our story at Sapphire.

Source: HBR — "To Scale AI Agents Successfully, Think of Them Like Team Members" (March 23, 2026)
